nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense was $50.9 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $7.7 million or 13.1%, compared to $58.6 million in the same period of 2025. This was primarily due to: (i) a decrease of 38 basis points in the total average rates of interest-bearing liabilities, primarily in the average rates paid on total deposits, FHLB advances, and Junior subordinated debentures; and (ii) a decrease of $174.9 million, or 8.4%, in the average balances of time deposits. These decreases were partially offset by an increase of $184.3 million, or 4.2% in the average balances of interest-bearing demand, savings and money market deposits.

Interest expense on interest-bearing deposits was $43.4 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $6.5 million, or 13.0%, compared to $49.9 million in the same period of 2025. This was mainly driven by a decrease of 40 basis points in the average rates paid on total deposits, partially offset by an increase of $9.4 million, or 0.1%, in their average balance. See below for a detailed explanation of changes by major deposit category:

• Time deposit s. Interest expense on total time deposits decreased $4.1 million, or 19.6%, in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. This was mainly due to a decrease of 49 basis points in the average rates paid on time deposits.

In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, income tax expense increased to $18.9 million from $14.5 million in the same period last year, primarily driven by higher income before income taxes in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period last year.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The table below sets forth information related to our income taxes for the periods presented.

In the third quarter of 2026, income tax expense increased to $7.8 million from $4.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, mainly driven by higher income before income taxes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year. In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, income tax expense increased to $18.9 million from $14.5 million in the same period last year, primarily driven by higher income before income taxes in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period last year.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s net deferred tax assets were $78.1 million, an increase of $42.6 million, or 119.6%, compared to $35.6 million as of December 31, 2025. This was primarily driven by an increase of $39.9 million in connection with $156.5 million in net unrealized holding losses on debt securities available for sale and, to a lesser extent, an increase in the allowance for credit losses and other smaller components during the period.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income. Net interest income represents interest income less interest expense. We generate interest income from interest, dividends and fees received on interest-earning assets, including loans and investment securities we own. We incur interest expense from interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities, including interest-bearing deposits, and borrowings such as advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank of Atlanta (“FHLB”) and other borrowings such as repurchase agreements, notes, debentures and other funding sources we may have from time to time. Net interest income typically is the most significant contributor to our revenues and net income. To evaluate net interest income, we measure and monitor: (i) yields on our loans and other interest-earning assets; (ii) the costs of our deposits and other funding sources; (iii) our net interest spread; (iv) our net interest margin, or NIM; and (v) our provisions for credit losses. Net interest spread is the difference between rates earned on interest-earning assets and rates paid on interest-bearing liabilities. NIM is calculated by dividing net interest income for the period by average interest-earning assets during that same period.

intro.text: We are a bank holding company headquartered in Coral Gables, FL, with $9.8 billion in assets, $6.6 billion in loans held for investment, $7.8 billion in deposits, $938.8 million of shareholders’ equity, and $3.3 billion in assets under management and custody (“AUM”) as of December 31, 2025. We provide individuals and businesses with a comprehensive array of deposit, credit, investment, wealth management, retail banking, mortgage services and fiduciary services. We serve customers in our United States markets and select international customers. These services are offered through our main subsidiary, Amerant Bank, N.A., or the Bank, which is also headquartered in Coral Gables, FL, as well as the Bank’s securities broker-dealer, Amerant Investments Inc., or Amerant Investments. Fiduciary, investment, wealth management and mortgage services are provided by the Bank and Amerant Investments.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.
